chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'The child is born with what is for men and with what is for women.' He said, 'It inherits from where its urine precedes. So if it comes out from both equally, then from where it spurts out. So if they are equal, it inherits the inheritance of men and women.'
ai.seo_question: How is the gender of a hermaphrodite determined for inheritance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the juristic methodology for determining the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite (ذو الخَلْقَيْنِ) by observing the primary urinary orifice, a principle rooted in the physical evidence of gender characteristics. If the exit is equal, the individual inherits the combined shares of both males and females, reflecting the Shia scholarly approach of balancing potential rights until definitive proof is established. This ruling highlights the practical application of empirical observation in Islamic inheritance law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The child was born with what is for the men and for it was what is for the women’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would inherit from where its urine precedes from. So if it comes out from both equally, so from where it spurts out (more strongly). So it was equal, it would inherit the inheritance of the men and the women’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a newborn who has the reproductive organs of both male and female. He (the Imam) said, ‘Such person inherits according to the reproductive organ from which urine comes first. If it comes from both at the same time then it is according to whichever sends with more pressure and if this is also equal then such person inherits the share of both male and female/”
